title: Highest-weight critical-exponent lower bound for the symmetric limit-set Hausdorff dimension of strongly projectively convex-cocompact subgroups of SL(n,R)
source_title: Hausdorff dimension of limit sets for projective Anosov representations
author: Olivier Glorieux; Daniel Monclair; Nicolas Tholozan
difficulty_reason: Coornaert’s visual-boundary dimension theorem alone does not compare the Euclidean dimension of the symmetric projective limit set with the highest-weight critical exponent. The authors prove a uniform primal-dual boundary estimate from Hilbert cross ratios, supporting hyperplanes and angle bounds, controlling both point and tangent-hyperplane distances. This new geometric comparison supplies the required dimension inequality before the formal entropy and Hausdorff-dimension conclusion.

proof_review.note: Full article retained as conservative closed context for notation, global assumptions, diagrams and references. Exact primary and supporting physical proof pages are recorded separately. Exact lower-bound Theorem3.1 only: strongly projectively convex-cocompact discrete subgroup of SL(n,R), hence a cocompact action on a nonempty convex core inside a Gromov-hyperbolic proper convex domain. Conclusion is2 delta_(1,n)<=Hausdorffdimension of the paired line-and-dual-hyperplane limit set, with any ambient smooth Riemannian metric. Preserve the factor2 from the half-log Hilbert-distance convention, not the weaker general Anosov corollary. Read complete new lower-bound30–34 and required new highest-weight entropy equality17–23, quantified proximal and conjugacy tools18–23, exact Cartan/critical definitions9–17 and Hilbert context25–29. DGK convex-core/boundary identification, Coornaert dimension theorem, Coornaert-Knieper counting and Guichard-Wienhard finite proximal perturbations are named prior foundations; original references retained. Elementary final uniform tangent-angle comparison33 is recorded after the authored affine cross-ratio/sine-law construction. Main two-sided statement not selected: upper-bound Lemma4.5 physical36 asserts forward invariance of the complement C_epsilon after proving forward invariance of its open complement, without a separate supporting argument; hold that upper-cover route instead of supplying a new semigroup argument. No tensor-product or surface-group specialization counted. Original PDF authors Olivier Glorieux/Daniel Monclair/Nicolas Tholozan and10/2023/241 verified.

historical_source_pdf_evidence.original_difficulty_reason: The author identifies Hilbert orbit growth with Cartan highest-weight growth through quantified proximal conjugacy counting, then compares the Gromov boundary quasi-distance with the geometric mean of primal and dual projective distances using tangent-plane cross-ratios. This higher-rank nonconformal boundary-dimension analysis exceeds qualifying examinations.
